headline: Record first-half profit, but full-year outlook trimmed

kpis.label: FY2026 total adjusted operating profit outlook

summary_short: Smithfield posted Q2 net sales of $3.7 billion (-2.3% y/y) but operating profit rose 11.6% y/y to $290 million as Packaged Meats and Hog Production offset softer Fresh Pork margins; the company then cut its FY2026 adjusted operating profit outlook to $1,225-$1,375 million from $1,325-$1,475 million.
summary_long: Record first-half operating profit ($623M, +7.1% y/y) masked a Q2 sales decline driven by non-recurring 2025 Hog Production JV sales and an earlier Easter. Packaged Meats operating profit fell 12.0% y/y to $265M as margin compressed 139bps to 13.1%, while Hog Production profit nearly tripled y/y on better hog markets. Net income rose 26.6% to $238M; adjusted diluted EPS rose 12.7% to $0.62. Cash stood at $1.35B with net debt/adjusted EBITDA of 0.4x; the board held the quarterly dividend at $0.3125/share ($1.25/share annualized). Management lowered FY2026 adjusted operating profit guidance across all three segments, citing cautious consumer spending and higher input costs, while holding capex ($350-450M) and the effective tax rate (22.5%-24.5%) unchanged.

drivers.explanation: Decline primarily due to non-recurring sales to Hog Production joint ventures in Q2 2025 and an earlier Easter holiday this year shifting seasonal demand.
Operating profit fell to $265M from $301M; margin compressed 139bps to 13.1%, though management said the segment remains highly profitable despite a tougher commodity backdrop.
Consolidated operating profit rose on a swing in Hog Production, whose profit nearly tripled y/y to $64M as the segment margin expanded 572bps, plus lower unallocated/corporate charges.
Net income growth outpaced operating profit growth, helped by higher non-operating gains ($17M vs $4M) and a lower effective tax rate versus the prior-year quarter.
Guidance was cut to reflect cautious consumer spending and higher input costs; management said the outlook change does not alter its view of brand strength or long-term earnings power.
